translation:
||Ramkabir||

||Prem-Bhakti-Prakash|| (Love, Devotion, Light)

_Jaise jaladhar unyo, badhat papaiya pyaas ||_
_Aise harijan aaye Jeevana, prem bhakti prakaash ||1||_
(As the rain-laden clouds swell, the papaiha bird's thirst grows all the more; so has the devotee of Hari come, O Jivan[ji] — the light of loving devotion.)

While engaged in discussion and satsang (holy discourse) with Guru Gopaldas, Jivanji Maharaj seeks to know the true nature (swarup) of Parbrahm (the Supreme Being). Gopaldasji explains the reconciliation (samanvay) of the formed (akar) and the formless (nirakar). Further explaining the nature of Parbrahm, he goes on to say that the truly real is the charming, flute-playing God (Morli Manohar Parmeshwar), whose names are Ram and Krishna. Finally, explaining the nature of Parbrahm in depth to Jivanji Maharaj, he says that the Word itself is God.

Only the Guru can grant the vision (darshan) of Parbrahm, but this darshan does not depend on any form or body — for whatever body or form takes birth is perishable, bound to be destroyed. But Parbrahm should be known only through name, or through words, for that alone is imperishable. Showing the way to reach the true nature of Parbrahm, Jivanji Maharaj explains it thus: just as, on seeing water-laden clouds grown wild with the urge to rain, the chatak bird's thirst to drink the cloud's water grows intense — in the very same way, devotees, through the flow of love-formed devotion (bhakti), can attain the radiant Brahm.

Love is of the nature of a flow (pravah). Just as water remains level and uniform at its surface — never more in one place and less in another, however high or low the ground beneath may be — water preserves equality at its upper surface, so too there can be no distinction among devotees; and only such devotees, free of distinction, can truly practise devotion. This is why love has been likened to the nature of water, and devotion (bhakti) to the nature of a bird — and it is only through the means of devotion that Parbrahm, who shines as radiantly as crores of suns, is to be attained. Thus it is only through the Guru's words — that is, through his Word — that He is to be known. This is why Jivanji Maharaj says: the Word itself is God.
